title: Some Roman concrete has lasted 2,000 years, and may even self-heal
body: Roman harbour walls and buildings like the Pantheon have stood for around two millennia. Their concrete mixed lime with volcanic ash, and in seawater this slowly grows a rare crystal, tobermorite, that may help it resist fracturing. A 2023 study also found that small lumps of lime, likely from mixing with hot quicklime, can react with water in cracks and reseal them. The ash also makes it more resistant to salt water than typical modern concrete.
